position_in_era.historical_role: The sister track to Estranged and the clearest public-facing statement of the Axl/Slash dual-protagonist dialectic. Multiple Slash guitar solos across nine minutes, each emerging as a response to a vocal section — the third solo, improvised during recording, is the song's emotional apex. NPR: 'one of the ultimate hard-rock power ballads.' The longest song to enter the top ten of the Billboard Hot 100 at the time.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Recorded at A&M Studios, Record Plant, and Conway Studios, Los Angeles (1990–1991). Orchestral string arrangement by Axl Rose. Duration: 8:57. Slash reported that his guitar solo on the album version 'developed directly from an improvisation' — a spontaneous statement that became the song's best-known solo passage. Three distinct guitar solos across the song.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Axl Rose (vocal, piano, string arrangement) and Slash (multiple lead guitar solos) as dual protagonists. Rose's orchestral arrangement frames the vocal as an aria — the strings supporting the voice. Slash's solos punctuate and respond to the vocal sections but also extend beyond them, claiming their own time. The complementary layering is documented: 'Rose's emotional vocal delivery frames the narrative while Slash's guitar passages expand the emotional landscape between and following vocal sections.'
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Slash: Les Paul through Marshall amp; the famous outdoor church performance in the video used a different (studio) take. Rose: piano, string synthesizer. Duff McKagan: bass. Matt Sorum: drums. Dizzy Reed: keyboards. Michael Kamen: orchestral arrangement.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Use Your Illusion I track 4. The music video (directed by Andy Morahan, 1992) became one of the most expensive ever made. The song's piano-to-orchestra structure explicitly positions it as a rock answer to operatic form.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Album September 1991; single June 1992 (US). Debuted at #3 on the Billboard Hot 100. At time of release, the longest charting top-ten hit in Hot 100 history.
